title: SM4, AES Inverse, and Camellia SBOX1 Boolean circuits: minimize total gates and multiplicative complexity
description: Sunstead pins OpenSSL's verbatim 256-entry tables (`openssl/openssl@d94024ff`, Apache-2.0) for three ISO/RFC/NIST standardized 8-bit cryptographic S-boxes — SM4 (RFC 8998 / ISO 18033-3), AES Inverse (NIST FIPS 197 §5.3.2), and Camellia SBOX1 (RFC 3713 / ISO 18033-3) — and kernel-proves byte-for-byte agreement with their algebraic GF(2^8) definitions on all 256 inputs in pure Lean 4.36.0 (no Mathlib). Six independent hill-climb tracks challenge contributors to minimize straight-line `{xor, xnor, and, not}` total gate count and multiplicative complexity (AND gate count) for each S-box.

tasks.title: SM4 S-box: minimize total gate count over {xor, xnor, and, not}
tasks.description: Submit a straight-line SM4 S-box circuit in CryptoSbox/Sm4TotalCircuit.lean (`sm4TotalScore`, `sm4TotalGates`, `sm4TotalOutputs`). The frozen Lean 4 kernel proof verifies well-formedness, gate count, and exact equivalence to RFC 8998 / ISO 18033-3 SM4 on all 256 inputs via `decide +kernel`. Only strict improvements below the current record earn credit.

tasks.title: SM4 S-box: minimize multiplicative complexity (AND gate count)
tasks.description: Submit a straight-line SM4 S-box circuit in CryptoSbox/Sm4AndCircuit.lean (`sm4AndScore`, `sm4AndGates`, `sm4AndOutputs`). The frozen Lean 4 kernel proof verifies well-formedness, AND gate count (`op == 2`), and exact equivalence to RFC 8998 / ISO 18033-3 SM4 on all 256 inputs via `decide +kernel`. Only strict improvements below the current record earn credit.
